points.t: A **firm, pink-brown, button-like papule** on a limb (often a woman’s lower leg) that **dimples when pinched**.
Benign reactive proliferation of **dermal fibroblasts and histiocytes**, sometimes after a bite or minor injury.
Clinical diagnosis + dermoscopy; **reassure**; excise only if symptomatic or uncertain (scar, may recur).
**DFSP** (growing, > 2–3 cm, trunk), **melanoma** (pigmented or changing), atypical dermoscopy.

cause.lead: A little knot of scar-like tissue.
points: Often after an insect bite, folliculitis or shaving nick.
Fibroblasts and histiocytes trap collagen; overlying epidermis thickens and pigments.
**Eruptive DFs** (≥ 15 or rapid): SLE, HIV, immunosuppressants, pregnancy.
Histology: **Factor XIIIa +, CD34 −** (the reverse of DFSP).
Firm dome-shaped pink-brown papule, < 1 cm usually; legs > arms.
**Dimple (Fitzpatrick) sign**: lateral pinch makes it dip inward.
Dermoscopy: **fine peripheral network + central white scar-like patch**.

visuals.caption: Dimple sign: squeezing the skin either side of a dermatofibroma makes it sink into a small pit, because it is tethered to the dermis.
visuals.alt: Fingers pinching leg skin around a small dimpling papule

points: Growth is still a 7-point major feature (2): document.
Explain the pinch test and benign nature; shaving guard if it catches.
NHS **Evidence-Based Interventions**: only for diagnostic doubt, recurrent bleeding / infection, function or significant pain.
Excision scar often bigger than the DF; recurrence if incomplete; cryo / shave leaves white mark (specialist / GP-surgeon decision).
Routine dermatology if uncertain or symptomatic; eruptive DFs on immunosuppressants: review drugs.

items.t: Changing pigmented lesion with atypical dermoscopy: suspected cancer pathway.
Growing beyond 2–3 cm, irregular, nodular or on the trunk: **DFSP**.

pearls.t: Teach the pinch test: “a little knot of scar-like tissue”.
Exam pair: DF Factor XIIIa + / CD34 −; DFSP the reverse.
Many new DFs: think SLE, HIV, immunosuppression.

quiz.a: Lateral pinch makes the papule dip inward.
Peripheral fine network + central white patch.

quiz.q: ‘DF’ growing to 4 cm on the chest?
